mF.stage: Upper Silurian (Ludlow-Pridoli; stage not given in source)

ill.why: quadrate zygospore type of the Mougeotia kind, recorded from the Palaeozoic (from general knowledge; check against the interval datasets)

mF.stage: Caradoc (Sandbian to early Katian), Late Ordovician

ill.why: naked permanent tetrahedral tetrad; spore bodies borne in tetrahedral tetrads are the embryophyte synapomorphy that Cambrian spore packets lack (Strother & Foster 2021 Science 373:792), and such tetrads occur inside Ordovician sporangia (Wellman et al. 2003)

CL.name: Bryophytes (Bryophyta sensu lato: hornworts, liverworts, mosses)

mF.stage: Lower Cretaceous (Koonwarra Fossil Bed; Aptian from general knowledge)

ill.why: named for its resemblance to Phaeoceros spores; no Palaeozoic hornwort spore type is accepted
Ordovician permanent tetrads with lamellate walls like some living liverworts (e.g. Sphaerocarpos tetrads, TTK ch. 5 p. 166); stem embryophyte vs liverwort affinity unresolved
the curvaturate, apiculate trilete type found in situ in both Rhynie protracheophytes

CL.name: Tracheophyta (vascular plants, Kenrick & Crane 1997 sense: Rhyniopsida + Eutracheophyta)
Rhyniophytes and rhyniophytoids (Rhyniopsida: Rhynia, Stockmansella, Huvenia, Sennicaulis; plus Cooksonia-type plants)

mF.stage: Wenlock (mid-Silurian; Homerian in the original report, from general knowledge)

ill.why: smooth, cingulate trilete spore found in situ in Silurian Cooksonia pertoni, and among the earliest trilete spore genera

mF.stage: Ludlow (Late Silurian; TTK: 'Siluro-Devonian rocks of Australia')

sF.stage: Lochkovian-Pragian (in situ records are Early Devonian)

ill.why: smooth curvaturate trilete spore found in situ in Zosterophyllum; TTK ch. 8 p. 252 warns that early trilete spores give few characters separating zosterophylls from rhyniophytes
smooth curvaturate trilete type of Asteroxylon, shared with zosterophylls: illustrates the zosterophyll-lycopsid transition
reticulate trilete type matching living Lycopodium; Palaeozoic in situ records for Lycopodiales are scarce (from general knowledge; not confirmed in Balme 1995)

CL.name: Isoetopsida (ligulate lycopsids: Selaginellales + Isoetales, with stem Protolepidodendrales)

ill.why: spiny trilete spores (60-85 µm) of the best-known protolepidodendrid Leclercqia (TTK p. 277)
zonate microspore found in situ in Carboniferous Selaginellites

CL.name: Isoetales sensu lato (Lepidodendrales, Pleuromeiales, Isoetaceae: rhizomorphic lycopsids)

ill.why: the small cingulate microspore of Lepidostrobus cones that dominates Pennsylvanian coal palynofloras of the arborescent lycopsids

CL.name: Euphyllophyta (ferns s.l., horsetails, seed plants and fossil stem relatives)

ill.why: in situ spore of trimerophytes, the earliest euphyllophytes; intact dispersed spores match A. brandtii Streel (Balme 1995 p. 96)

CL.name: Trimerophytes (Psilophyton, Pertica, Trimerophyton; paraphyletic stem euphyllophytes)

ill.why: A. brandtii-type spores are the in situ spore of Psilophyton (Balme 1995 p. 96)

CL.name: Monilophyta (ferns s.l. = PPG I Polypodiopsida, plus fossil stem groups)

ill.why: large biformate trilete spore in situ in Foozia and Calamophyton, Emsian-Middle Devonian (Balme 1995 p. 136)

CL.name: 'Coenopterid' ferns: Zygopteridales and Stauropteridales (not a clade)

ill.why: distinctive stauropterid megaspore tetrad (two functional + two aborted spores), Lower Carboniferous; zygopterid miospores (verrucate, convolute, spinose trilete) are not diagnostic (Balme 1995 p. 136)

CL.name: Sphenopsida / Equisetidae total group (Sphenophyllales + Equisetales; also Pseudoborniales)

ill.why: hilate perisporate trilete spore found in both sphenophyll and calamitean cones (Balme 1995 summary)
Balme 1995 p. 123: hilate trilete bowmanitalean spores = Vestispora, a useful Carboniferous index
trilete spore with three elaters, the fossil counterpart of the elaterate spores of living Equisetum (TTK ch. 10 p. 367)

CL.name: Ophioglossidae + Marattiidae + Polypodiidae (unnamed: all ferns except horsetails)
Ophioglossidae (Ophioglossales: moonworts, adder's-tongues; Psilotales: whisk ferns)

ill.why: the only in situ link (Paleocene Botrychium); no Paleozoic record

CL.name: Marattiales (Psaronius-Scolecopteris tree ferns and living Marattiaceae)

ill.why: Balme 1995 summary names Torispora among the few dispersed genera reliable at order level (Marattiales); characteristic of Late Carboniferous tree-fern spore floras

CL.name: Polypodiidae (leptosporangiate ferns), with Paleozoic filicalean families

ill.why: baculate trilete spore in situ in Paleozoic filicalean ferns (Tedeleaceae) and botryopterids/zygopterids (Balme summary)
granulate-baculate trilete spore in situ in Late Permian Todites (TTK p. 441)
cavate trilete spore of the earliest (Eifelian) aneurophytalean progymnosperms
large cavate trilete spore of the earliest aneurophytes; common Eifelian-Frasnian
Archaeopteris microspore whose Givetian-Frasnian abundance records the first forests
earliest dispersed megaspores matching seed megaspores

CL.name: Devonian hydrasperman seed plants (Elkinsia, Moresnetia, Archaeosperma, Hydrasperma, Xenotheca; paraphyletic)

ill.why: early seed-plant prepollen is optically indistinguishable from pteridophyte spores (Balme 1995 p. 188), so the seed habit is invisible palynologically
